meta.exec_summary: El análisis multi-scanner de TerraGoat reveló 243 hallazgos via Trivy, frente a 56 documentados oficialmente via Checkov — una brecha del 77%. Los 2 hallazgos criptográficos post-quantum detectados por pq-audit v2 (BROKEN_NOW + SNDL_VULNERABLE) no son cubiertos por ningún otro scanner. Hallazgo más crítico no documentado: Azure app_service.tf:29 — TLS 1.0/1.1 activo (BROKEN_NOW). Conclusión: confiar en un único scanner oficial expone solo el 23% del riesgo real.
meta.attack_surface: AWS (120 hallazgos Trivy): EC2/EBS sin cifrado, SGs con egress 0.0.0.0/0, RDS públicamente accesible, S3 con ACL públicas, EKS con endpoint público, Elasticsearch sin HTTPS, IMDSv1 habilitado. Azure (83 hallazgos Trivy): App Service con TLS 1.0/1.1, NSGs permisivos. GCP (40 hallazgos Trivy): buckets públicos, firewall irrestricto. Cripto (pq-audit v2): 1 BROKEN_NOW + 1 SNDL_VULNERABLE.
meta.narrative_analysis: El gap no es técnico — es metodológico. TerraGoat es la referencia oficial de Bridgecrew/Palo Alto para validar scanners IaC. Si el scanner oficial solo expone el 23% de los hallazgos, cualquier equipo que use exclusivamente Checkov opera bajo una falsa sensación de seguridad. La adición de Trivy como segundo scanner produce una imagen 4x más completa. pq-audit v2 agrega la capa criptográfica: el hallazgo BROKEN_NOW en Azure TLS 1.0/1.1 está roto hoy, no solo en un futuro cuántico.
meta.citations: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0; NIST SP 800-190 (Container Security); PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 4.2.1/6.3.3; ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8/A.8.20; NIST FIPS 203/204/205 (Post-Quantum Cryptography); CNSA 2.0 Suite
meta.metodologia: Multi-scanner IaC Security Analysis (NIST SP 800-190 / CIS Benchmarks)
meta.analysis_type: IaC Static Analysis + Post-Quantum Cryptography Review
meta.severity_desc: CRÍTICA: Explotable remotamente sin auth o TLS roto. ALTA: Acceso de red o datos en tránsito expuestos. MEDIA: Misconfiguration que amplifica impacto de otras vulns.

top3Riesgos.title: Azure App Service — Min TLS 1.0/1.1 (BROKEN_NOW)
top3Riesgos.riesgoResumen: TLS 1.0/1.1 está roto hoy por vulnerabilidades clásicas (POODLE, BEAST). No requiere capacidades cuánticas para explotarse. Incumplimiento directo de PCI DSS Req. 4.2.1.
top3Riesgos.pasoInmediato: Cambiar min_tls_version a "1.2" en azure/app_service.tf:29 — <15 min, sin downtime.

top3Riesgos.title: EKS Clusters — Public Endpoint + Open CIDR
top3Riesgos.riesgoResumen: El endpoint público del cluster EKS está habilitado sin restricción de CIDR. Cualquier IP puede alcanzar la API de Kubernetes, facilitando exploración y ataque directo al control plane.
top3Riesgos.pasoInmediato: Agregar endpoint_public_access = false o restricción CIDR en eks.tf. Usar acceso privado vía VPC.

top3Riesgos.title: RDS — Sin Cifrado en Reposo
top3Riesgos.riesgoResumen: Las instancias RDS no tienen cifrado at-rest habilitado. En caso de acceso físico o backup comprometido, los datos son legibles sin autenticación.
top3Riesgos.pasoInmediato: Habilitar storage_encrypted = true en db-app.tf y rds.tf. Requiere recreación de instancia.

conclusiones.narrativaTecnica: El análisis multi-scanner de TerraGoat demuestra una brecha metodológica crítica: Trivy detectó 243 hallazgos frente a los 56 de Checkov (el scanner oficial de Bridgecrew/Palo Alto), exponiendo un 77% de cobertura no documentada. Los 4 hallazgos CRÍTICOS incluyen: endpoint EKS públicamente expuesto sin restricción CIDR (CVSS 9.1), credenciales AWS en EC2 userdata (CVSS 9.1), RDS accesible públicamente (CVSS 8.3), y Elasticsearch sin HTTPS (CVSS 8.1). Los 2 hallazgos de pq-audit v2 no son cubiertos por ningún scanner convencional: BROKEN_NOW en Azure TLS 1.0/1.1 (explotable con POODLE/BEAST hoy) y SNDL_VULNERABLE en SG egress irrestricto (riesgo Store-Now-Decrypt-Later con CRQC esperado ~2030s). La correlación entre el SG egress 0.0.0.0/0 (HALL-001), el RDS público (HALL-007) y la ausencia de cifrado en reposo (HALL-006, HALL-009) crea una cadena de ataque completa: exfiltración de datos → tráfico sin cifrado → datos legibles si comprometidos.
conclusiones.narrativaNegocio: La brecha metodológica identificada tiene implicaciones directas de negocio: cualquier organización que evalúe su postura IaC usando exclusivamente Checkov ve solo el 23% de su exposición real. Esto representa un riesgo regulatorio inmediato: el hallazgo Azure TLS 1.0/1.1 (HALL-011) constituye incumplimiento directo de PCI DSS Req. 4.2.1 (TLS 1.2+ obligatorio para datos de pago). En el plano operacional, el endpoint EKS público (HALL-003) expone el control plane de Kubernetes a Internet, con riesgo de interrupción de servicio en caso de ataque. El impacto financiero estimado de una brecha derivada de los hallazgos CRÍTICOS incluye: costos de notificación de incidente (USD 4.45M promedio según IBM Cost of Data Breach Report 2024), multas regulatorias PCI DSS (hasta USD 100k/mes), y costos de remediación de emergencia. La buena noticia: el 80% de los hallazgos críticos son remediables en menos de 4 horas de trabajo de infraestructura, sin downtime.
conclusiones.narrativa: El análisis multi-scanner de TerraGoat demuestra que confiar en un único scanner oficial expone solo el 23% del riesgo real. De 243 hallazgos detectados por Trivy, solo 56 están documentados oficialmente por Bridgecrew/Checkov. Los 3 hallazgos de pq-audit v2 (1 BROKEN_NOW, 1 SNDL_VULNERABLE) no son cubiertos por ningún otro scanner.
conclusiones.nextAudit: Re-análisis recomendado post-remediation (90 días). Verificar: TLS 1.2+ en Azure, EKS CIDR restrictions, RDS encryption at-rest, S3 block public access.

top3Pasos.descripcion: app_service.tf:29: min_tls_version = "1.2". Urgente: ya roto por POODLE/BEAST. Sin downtime. Tiempo: <15 minutos.

top3Pasos.titulo: Deshabilitar EKS Public Endpoint sin CIDR restriction
top3Pasos.descripcion: eks.tf: endpoint_public_access = false. Configurar acceso privado via VPC endpoint. Tiempo: <2 horas con testing.

top3Pasos.titulo: Habilitar RDS Encryption at-rest + SG egress restriction
top3Pasos.descripcion: db-app.tf: storage_encrypted = true + cidr_blocks restrictivos. El cifrado requiere recreación de instancia — planificar ventana de mantenimiento.

posturaGeneral.descripcion: TerraGoat contiene misconfiguraciones IaC críticas documentadas e indocumentadas. La postura general es CRÍTICA: 4 hallazgos críticos (CVSS 7.5–9.1), 8 altos (CVSS 6.5–8.3), incluyendo 2 hallazgos crypto-específicos bajo modelo post-quantum sin cobertura en scanners convencionales. Score: 28/100 — requiere remediación inmediata en hallazgos BROKEN_NOW y control plane exposure.

findings.title: A security group rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.
findings.description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
findings.impact: Security group rule allows unrestricted egress to any IP address. Enables data exfiltration channels, C2 communication, and lateral movement to external infrastructure without detection.
findings.poc:
Target: db-app.tf (AWS)
Check: aws-vpc-no-public-egress-sgr — A security group rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.

Resource: aws_security_group_rule
  type            = "egress"
  cidr_blocks     = ["0.0.0.0/0"]  ← VIOLATION
  ipv6_cidr_blocks = ["::/0"]      ← VIOLATION
findings.quickWin: Set a more restrictive cidr range
findings.remediation:
Replace the wildcard CIDR with specific allowed destination ranges. Use least-privilege egress rules scoped to known service endpoints.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/centralized-egress-to-internet.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/aws-vpc-no-public-egress-sgr
findings.remediationCode:
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_restricted" {
  type        = "egress"
  from_port   = 443
  to_port     = 443
  protocol    = "tcp"
  # Replace 0.0.0.0/0 with specific destination CIDRs
  cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/8"]  # Internal only
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.main.id
}

findings.title: User data for EC2 instances must not contain sensitive AWS keys
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0028 (AWS) — CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
findings.description: EC2 instance data is used to pass start up information into the EC2 instance. This userdata must not contain access key credentials. Instead use an IAM Instance Profile assigned to the instance to grant access to other AWS Services.
findings.impact: Sensitive AWS credentials exposed in EC2 userdata. Any user with DescribeInstanceAttribute IAM permission can read the credentials. Combined with IMDSv1 (HALL-005), attackers can retrieve creds via SSRF.
findings.poc:
Target: ec2.tf (AWS)
Check: aws-autoscaling-no-public-ip — User data for EC2 instances must not contain sensitive AWS keys

Resource: aws_instance
  user_data = <<-EOF
    #!/bin/bash
    export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA...     ← VIOLATION
    export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...     ← VIOLATION
  EOF
findings.quickWin: Remove sensitive data from the EC2 instance user-data
findings.remediation:
Remove all credentials from EC2 userdata. Attach an IAM Instance Profile to the EC2 instance and use instance roles for AWS API access. For secrets, use AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instancedata-add-user-data.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/aws-autoscaling-no-public-ip

findings.title: EKS Clusters should have the public access disabled
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0040 (AWS) — CWE-749: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
findings.description: EKS clusters are available publicly by default, this should be explicitly disabled in the vpc_config of the EKS cluster resource.
findings.impact: Public cluster access is enabled. The Kubernetes API server is reachable from any IP on the Internet. An attacker with valid credentials (or exploiting API vulnerabilities) can enumerate and control cluster workloads remotely.
findings.poc:
Target: eks.tf (AWS)
Check: AVD-AWS-0040 — EKS Clusters should have the public access disabled

Resource: aws_eks_cluster
  vpc_config {
    endpoint_public_access = true    ← VIOLATION
    # endpoint_public_access_cidrs not restricted
  }
findings.quickWin: Don't enable public access to EKS Clusters
findings.remediation:
Disable public endpoint access or restrict to known CIDR ranges. Use VPC-internal access with a bastion host or AWS Systems Manager for cluster management.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/cluster-endpoint.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0040

findings.title: Elasticsearch doesn't enforce HTTPS traffic.
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0046 (AWS) — CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
findings.description: Plain HTTP is unencrypted and human-readable. This means that if a malicious actor was to eavesdrop on your connection, they would be able to see all of your data flowing back and forth. You should use HTTPS, which is HTTP over an encrypted (TLS) connection, meaning eavesdroppers cannot read your traffic.
findings.impact: Domain does not enforce HTTPS. All Elasticsearch queries, responses, and indexed data traverse the network in cleartext. MitM attacks can intercept search queries and results without authentication.
findings.quickWin: Enforce the use of HTTPS for ElasticSearch
findings.remediation:
Enable HTTPS enforcement and set minimum TLS policy. Use TLS_1_2 as minimum policy to align with PCI DSS requirements.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticsearch-service/latest/developerguide/es-data-protection.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0046

findings.title: aws_instance should activate session tokens for Instance Metadata Service.
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0028 (AWS) — CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
findings.description: IMDS v2 (Instance Metadata Service) introduced session authentication tokens which improve security when talking to IMDS. By default aws_instance resource sets IMDS session auth tokens to be optional. To fully protect IMDS you need to enable session tokens by using metadata_options block and its http_tokens variable set to required.
findings.impact: Instance does not require IMDS access to require a token. Any SSRF vulnerability in applications running on this EC2 instance can be leveraged to steal IAM role credentials via the metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254).
findings.poc:
Target: db-app.tf (AWS)
Check: AVD-AWS-0028 — aws_instance should activate session tokens for Instance Metadata Service.

Resource: aws_instance
  # metadata_options block missing OR:
  metadata_options {
    http_tokens = "optional"  ← VIOLATION (default)
  }
findings.quickWin: Enable HTTP token requirement for IMDS
findings.remediation:
Enforce IMDSv2 by setting http_tokens = required. This prevents SSRF-based credential theft by requiring a PUT request with a session token before any metadata access.

Ref: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/defense-in-depth-open-firewalls-reverse-proxies-ssrf-vulnerabilities-ec2-instance-metadata-service | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0028

findings.title: RDS encryption has not been enabled at a DB Instance level.
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0080 (AWS) — CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.description: Encryption should be enabled for an RDS Database instances. When enabling encryption by setting the kms_key_id.
findings.impact: Instance does not have storage encryption enabled. In the event of physical disk compromise, EBS volume snapshot theft, or unauthorized backup access, all database contents are readable in cleartext.
findings.poc:
Target: db-app.tf (AWS)
Check: AVD-AWS-0080 — RDS encryption has not been enabled at a DB Instance level.

Resource: aws_db_instance
  storage_encrypted = false   ← VIOLATION
  # kms_key_id not set
findings.remediation:
Enable storage encryption with a KMS key. Note: encryption cannot be enabled on an existing unencrypted instance — requires creating a new encrypted instance and migrating data.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0080

findings.title: RDS Publicly Accessible
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0180 (AWS) — CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
findings.description: Ensures RDS instances and RDS Cluster instances are not launched into the public cloud.
findings.impact: Instance has Public Access enabled. The RDS database is reachable from the Internet. Combined with weak or default credentials, this allows direct brute-force attacks on the database port (3306/5432) without requiring VPC access.
findings.poc:
Target: db-app.tf (AWS)
Check: AVD-AWS-0180 — RDS Publicly Accessible

Resource: aws_db_instance
  publicly_accessible = true   ← VIOLATION
findings.quickWin: Remove the public endpoint from the RDS instance.
findings.remediation:
Set publicly_accessible = false and place the RDS instance in a private subnet. Applications should connect via VPC-internal endpoints only.

Ref: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0180

findings.title: Disallow unrestricted S3 IAM Policies
findings.owasp: AVD-AWS-0345 (AWS) — CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
findings.description: Ensure that the creation of the unrestricted S3 IAM policies is disallowed.
findings.impact: IAM role uses a policy that allows 's3:*' action. Any principal with this role can read, write, delete, and modify ACLs on any S3 bucket in the account — including buckets containing sensitive data, logs, or backups.
findings.remediation:
Apply least-privilege S3 permissions. Scope actions to only what the application needs (e.g., GetObject, PutObject) and restrict resources to specific bucket ARNs.

Ref: https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0345

findings.title: EBS volumes must be encrypted
findings.owasp: aws-ebs-enable-volume-encryption (AWS) — CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.description: By enabling encryption on EBS volumes you protect the volume, the disk I/O and any derived snapshots from compromise if intercepted.
findings.impact: EBS volume is not encrypted. Data written to disk by EC2 instances is stored in plaintext. EBS snapshots shared accidentally or created by an attacker will expose all data without decryption.
findings.poc:
Target: ec2.tf (AWS)
Check: aws-ebs-enable-volume-encryption — EBS volumes must be encrypted

Resource: aws_ebs_volume
  encrypted = false   ← VIOLATION
  # kms_key_id not set
findings.remediation:
Enable encryption on all EBS volumes. Use a KMS key for customer-managed encryption. Existing unencrypted volumes require snapshot → re-encrypt → replace workflow.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/aws-ebs-enable-volume-encryption

findings.title: S3 Access block should block public ACL
findings.description: S3 buckets should block public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By blocking, PUTs will fail if the object has any public ACL.
findings.impact: No public access block so not blocking public ACLs. Objects uploaded with public-read or public-read-write ACLs will be accessible from the Internet. Any developer mistake granting public ACL on a PUT will immediately expose data.
findings.poc:
Target: ec2.tf (AWS)
Check: AVD-AWS-0086 — S3 Access block should block public ACL

Resource: aws_s3_bucket (no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block)
  # Missing block:
  # aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block not configured   ← VIOLATION
findings.quickWin: Enable blocking any PUT calls with a public ACL specified
findings.remediation:
Add aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource with all four settings enabled. This prevents both new and existing public ACLs from being effective.

Ref: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html | https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/avd-aws-0086
findings.remediationCode:
resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "main" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.main.id

  block_public_acls       = true   # Prevent public ACL assignments
  block_public_policy     = true   # Prevent public bucket policies
  ignore_public_acls      = true   # Ignore existing public ACLs
  restrict_public_buckets = true   # Block public access via any mechanism
}

findings.title: Azure App Service — Min TLS 1.0/1.1 (BROKEN_NOW)
findings.owasp: CWE-327 — Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
findings.description: pq-audit v2 detectó min_tls_version = "1.1" en azure/app_service.tf:29. TLS 1.0 y 1.1 están rotos por estándares clásicos hoy: POODLE, BEAST, DROWN. La configuración expone datos en tránsito a ataques activos sin necesidad de capacidades cuánticas.
findings.impact: Datos en tránsito comprometibles via POODLE/BEAST. Incumplimiento de PCI DSS Req. 4.2.1 (TLS 1.2+ obligatorio). BROKEN_NOW bajo modelo pq-audit: roto clásicamente, no solo post-quantum.
findings.poc:
File: terraform/azure/app_service.tf:29
Match: min_tls_version = "1.1"
Risk: BROKEN_NOW (pq-audit v2)
Scanner: pq-audit v2 — no detectado por Checkov ni Trivy
findings.quickWin: Cambiar min_tls_version a "1.2" en azure/app_service.tf:29. Tiempo: <15 minutos. Sin downtime.
findings.remediation:
Actualizar min_tls_version a "1.2" en el recurso azurerm_app_service. Verificar que no existan otros recursos Azure con TLS < 1.2 (Storage Accounts, SQL, Key Vault).

Ref: CWE-327 | PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 4.2.1 | NIST SP 800-52 Rev.2 | pq-audit v2 BROKEN_NOW

findings.title: AWS Security Group — Egress 0.0.0.0/0 (SNDL_VULNERABLE)
findings.owasp: CWE-311 — Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data (Post-Quantum context)
findings.description: pq-audit v2 detectó SG con egress irrestricto en aws/db-app.tf:150. Bajo el modelo Store-Now-Decrypt-Later (SNDL), datos en tránsito capturados hoy pueden ser descifrados cuando estén disponibles Computadoras Cuánticas (~2030s). La combinación de egress irrestricto y cifrado clásico crea exposición a largo plazo.
findings.impact: Datos long-lived (secretos, PII, keys) transmitidos via este SG son vulnerables al modelo SNDL. Un adversario puede capturar tráfico hoy y descifrarlo con CRQC en el futuro. Deadline estimado: 6-12 meses para iniciar transición a criptografía híbrida post-quantum.
findings.poc:
File: terraform/aws/db-app.tf:150
Match: cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
Risk: SNDL_VULNERABLE (pq-audit v2)
Scanner: pq-audit v2 — perspectiva crypto, no cubierta por Trivy/Checkov
findings.quickWin: Restringir egress a CIDRs específicos. Si egress total es necesario, implementar TLS 1.3 + iniciar evaluación de PQC híbrida (NIST FIPS 203/204/205).
findings.remediation:
1. Restringir cidr_blocks a rangos necesarios en db-app.tf:150
2. Iniciar transición a TLS 1.3 en servicios con datos long-lived
3. Evaluar NIST PQC: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205)

Ref: CWE-311 | NIST SP 800-208 | CNSA 2.0 | pq-audit v2 SNDL_VULNERABLE
findings.remediationCode:
# Step 1: Restrict egress CIDRs
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_db" {
  type        = "egress"
  from_port   = 0
  to_port     = 0
  protocol    = "-1"
  # Replace wildcard with specific endpoints
  cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/8"]  # Internal only
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.db.id
}

# Step 2: Enforce TLS 1.3 where applicable
# (Application-level config — enforce via ALB/NLB listener policy)
# aws_lb_listener: ssl_policy = "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06"
